speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am the parent of an adult with moderate autism.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I actively volunteer at and head a couple of disability organisations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am also a Member of Parliament and Mayor involved in disability support initiatives as one of my duties.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I therefore view past, current and future developments in this sector from many perspectives.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My feelings are mixed – a mix of joy, a mix of concern and a mix of cautious optimism.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Today, I want to propose five changes that need to happen before persons with disabilities can fully participate in the life of Singapore society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But first, let me touch on the positive developments, thanks to the Singapore Government, in the last 15 years.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The calls for the inclusion of PwDs in Singapore society are as old as time, especially in 2004, after Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong's inauguration, that the disability sector became a lot more visible at the national level.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In the last 15 years, much has been achieved.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Singapore became a signatory to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, which it ratified in 2013.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These are big steps toward ensuring the rights for PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What were most significant to me personally were the following milestones: the commissioning of three five-year Enabling Masterplans for the disabled – a blueprint to chart the sector's vision and plans; substantial increase in Government funding of Early Intervention Centres and special schools; the setting up of SG Enable, an agency for the disability community and an Enabling Village, a physical hub to assemble services; the introduction of universal coverage for MediShield Life, a basic health insurance plan which now includes persons with pre-existing conditions; and schemes to incentivise employers to hire PwDs; and, to me, very importantly, the waiver for headcount quota to encourage the hiring of PwDs in the public service.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am optimistic that positive changes will continue and 4G advocates like Rahayu Mahzam, Cheryl Chan, Ang Wei Neng, Sun Xueling, Darryl David and many others will rise to the occasion and continue to seek the inclusion of PwDs in our society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Even as we have good reasons to pat ourselves on our backs, we know something is still amiss.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One has only to listen to the feedback of one focus group after another of PwDs and their family care-givers and also observe the outcomes in living, learning and working of the PwDs to know that we are not quite there yet.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In community awareness and support, both the Lien Foundation and the NCSS have reported the state of social inclusion and stigma.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many social service offices, family service centres or FSCs, grassroots organisations and community centres are not yet part of the support network of PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many people still not heard about the Enabling Village or the many awareness programmes and campaigns, that are being conducted over these years.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: On care-giver worries, families continue to fret over what will happen to their children upon the demise of the parents – a classic concern.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The feelings of helplessness are even more prevalent in families where children have multiple or more severe disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The needs of family care-givers change over the life cycle, same as for those with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There appears to be lacking a robust care-giver support model that is more empowering, more family-based and more community-based.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In living, there are challenges in daily living matters.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many PwDs are not prepared for independent living as adults.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Not many are trained from young to adopt a healthy lifestyle, leading quite a bit to premature chronic illnesses that add to their disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In health insurance coverage, accounting graduate Wesley Loh recently highlighted the challenges of getting himself covered for life insurance.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Wesley was either turned down or offered coverage with a whole load of exclusions because he had declared his diagnosis of autism.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: He is not alone in being turned down by insurers for insurance applications.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In residential living, adults with disabilities have very few options.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The choices that other Singaporeans enjoy are not theirs to have and supported living options are not always available.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In learning, for many special school or SPED students, graduation is not an occasion for joy.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Most SPED students stop learning, whether in daily living or at work.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The cliff effect phenomenon for SPED students is well known and describes the fall to little or no services for these students after they complete their formal years of school at usually age 18.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This could be a syndrome that is due to the way services and budgets are planned and resourced in silos, based on Government Ministries.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Lifelong learning, the holy grail of Singapore's SkillsFuture movement, is a pipe dream for many adults with disabilities, primarily because most SkillsFuture offerings are inaccessible without the needed disability support.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In the world of work, unemployment and under-employment are two big concerns.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Under-employment continues to be an issue for those who are cognitively able on the spectrum.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many PwDs are still not ready for work when they leave school and there are still not enough employers who are confident enough to employ and to develop them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Now, the gaps and challenges I highlighted just now are not limited to Singapore and arise basically due to a combination of factors which include perspectives, structures and provisions.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One, society's view of persons with disabilities needs to change.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One of the young people I serve with in my volunteer work is 31-year-old Dr Sim Zi Lin, a millennial.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Zi Lin completed her PhD in a renowned American university before returning to Singapore to work in a special school.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Zi Lin used to share how in her overseas study stint, she was often struck by the expectation that it is the duty of the university to provide for the removal of any barriers to participation to learning for undergrads who are disabled.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Just do it – expected; even if things were not always perfect.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Zi Lin also shared with me in our work in enabling PwDs how she notices PwDs, her peers, have far fewer choices and pathways in life compared to their typical peers.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And I believe a lot of it has to do with how society views PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For many years, the most common views of society towards PwDs are based on two traditional models – the medical model and the charity model.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The medical model sees disabled persons primarily as persons who need to be "cured", who need to be made "normal".

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And the charity model sees disabled people as victims of life, deserving of pity and need charity so that they can survive.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But there is another thinking model that many progressive countries adopt in viewing PwDs – that disability is the consequence of attitudinal, environmental and social barriers and hence, the removal of these barriers would enable PwDs to participate fully in the life of the community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The good news is that something is already happening for yet another population – the elderly people of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We see fantastic work by MOH and partners in many policies and programmes related to the seniors – active ageing and eldercare.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For instance, a growing school of thought that seniors with dementia should be treated respectfully as equal members of society and supported by a surrounding dementia-friendly community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I watched with marvel the way a home nursing staff apologised and explained to my mother – she is no more around.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I marvelled at the steps that this nurse would take, even when my mother, who had full-blown Alzheimer's, could not respond to her at all.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Mom was treated with such respect and gentleness.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, the perspective that even if one were old and ailing, one should still be treated respectfully and not lose the opportunity to make choices, to be developed or to contribute.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This new attitude towards ageing Singaporeans is progressive, it is liberating and reflected in corresponding responses in Singapore's community, policy, services and Budget planning – a very good learning example for the younger disabled community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It becomes natural that we adopt universal design or design for all, in policies and practices at the start, whether in designing physical facilities or services.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Meaning, independence and dignity for all, abled or disabled.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Two, gaps in provisions for PwDs need to be addressed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The gap analysis ought to be undertaken, hopefully before the next Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I will list just a few newer suggestions for consideration to improve living, learning and working outcomes for the PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In living, let us strengthen public communications through a total strategic plan to ensure that PwDs will receive the same level of information on matters that impact them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We should ensure that there are provisions to make sure that they have security, safety and access to criminal justice.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Develop a plan to bring a continuum of sustainable, integrated residential living options with all levels of needed support.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Empower them and their care-givers with a more comprehensive support plan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Someone taught me, what we call, "life after death" – planning, developing a "playbook" of planning for life after death of the care-givers to ensure that the PwDs have continuity in life.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Set up partnerships so that there is a fully array of accessible SkillsFuture offerings.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Resource SG Enable and their service providers, or partners better, to include a newer definition of work in the new economy, continuum of employment models and upskilling PwDs, employers, training providers and job coaches.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Number three, performance and progress need to be reported and readily available.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There ought to be a study of the most effective ways to ensure that this information reaches out, on an on-going basis, to the people who are affected by this news, progress or updates.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: People must know what is going on before they know where to get help.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Volunteers and help agencies too, they need to know what is going on before they start their pet projects which if they do not know, will lead to an overlaps in services, so that gaps which are critical will not be overlooked.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Four, structure for policy-making and services, the need to drive collaboration and the spirit of SG Together which Deputy Prime Minister Heng spoke so much about.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The "Many-Helping-Hands" approach has long been adopted for disability services in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It, of course, has its proponents and detractors.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are some who believe that Government does everything best, must take over everything.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Others feel that the users of services, the PwDs themselves or the disability service providers, know what is best.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They are on the ground and they believe they should be the ones who lead and implement changes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I believe the answer is neither here nor there.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Government alone cannot drive and deliver all the changes we need to reach the vision of full participation of PwDs in our society.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Mind you, I have worked with very amazing, very visionary civil servants before.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But the role and natural DNA of Government tends to be to "govern" and dare I say, "control", depending on who is in charge at the moment, at that time.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And that is how sometimes terms like "bureaucrats" are used, either by civil servants themselves or by their detractors.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The truth of the matter is that such visioning amongst such different partners, this kind of alliance, will not be an easy alliance at the start.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: PwDs, families, political leaders, Government leaders, civil servants, social service agencies, they are all at different levels of awareness, maturity, motivation and competence.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But alliance it has to be for this sector especially, for positive change and long-term impact.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Each one has to take our place, doing our part with both courage and consideration.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And finally, the voice of people disabilities need to be included.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: People with disabilities are not all the same.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some will have higher support needs, more severe and their family care-givers sometimes become their proxies.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Others like the vice-chairmen and members of this year's Purple Parade Committee – it is an inclusive movement: Yip Pin Xiu , Alistair Ong and Eric Chen – they have their own views and they do not need another to represent them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Eric Chen, in a recent letter to the Forum, urged Singapore to empower PwDs to stand as equals.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: He cited, "Many of us understand inclusion as a dependent relationship where abled people are responsible for supporting people who are disabled and to integrate them into mainstream." Eric then said that, "PwDs are seen as being unable to contribute meaningfully to determine their own future; and plans are undertaken by abled people on their behalf".

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: He asked for Government to form – and these are his words – to form an "alliance with service providers, including employers, care-givers and disabled people" so that disabled people too can form part of the inclusion blueprint.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Not every PwD will make a good leader.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But that goes for the rest of us.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: To do this, I summarise five changes need to happen.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One, society's view of PwDs has to change.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Two, gaps in provisions need to be addressed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Three, performance and progress must be no secret – they need to be reported and readily available.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Four, the structure for policy-making and services need to drive collaboration and spirit of SG Together.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And five, the voice of PwDs need to be included.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: That was a very structured and inspirational speech.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: And may I call on Minister of State Sun Xueling to respond, please.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Ms Phua that we should take a life-cycle approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since the first five-year Enabling Masterplans, in 2007, we have progressively put in place more support for PwDs at every stage of life and have strived to smoothen the transition between life stages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will share some progress made over the years in areas raised by Ms Phua.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I know that more needs to be done and we hope to continue our journey with our partners to make further improvements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, in the area of education and transitioning to post-school life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As mentioned by Ms Phua, there has been progress in the area of early intervention, with more development and learning support in pre-schools and intervening earlier through EIPIC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To prepare Special Education or SPED school students for life, MOE works closely with the Social Service Agencies or SSAs that run the schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE has strengthened vocational education for SPED, and is also working with SPED schools to further customise curriculums in seven learning domains, including social emotional skills and digital literacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree that the transition from the structured school environment to post-school options can be challenging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To help students and families navigate post-school pathways, there are now Transition Planning Coordinators in all SPED schools serving Secondary-aged students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MOE will be releasing an Individual Planning Guide to help develop person-centred plans for each student's schooling journey, and their transition to adult life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: All SPED schools serving students up to 18 years old also offer the School-to-Work transition programme, which offers customised training pathways and work options to eligible students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, strengthening support for PwDs in the post schooling years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the area of lifelong learning, SkillsFuture Singapore, or SSG, has been working with training providers to offer courses, like customised Digital Workplaces courses, for PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SSG and SG Enable are also expanding the range of industry-relevant SkillsFuture credit-eligible courses for PwDs, and have also introduced SkillsFuture Study Awards for PwDs and disability employment professionals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the area of healthcare, MINDS received Government funding to open a clinic offering primary care and preventative health services to persons with intellectual disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over 60 dental clinics across Singapore have general dental practitioners trained in special needs dentistry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Active living is also an important part of health promotion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have made sports facilities and programming more accessible under the Disability Sports Masterplan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the area of insurance coverage, MediShield Life covers all Singaporeans and Permanent Residents for life, including congenital conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Ms Phua mentioned, MSF and MAS are looking to issue guidelines for insurers to treat PwDs the same as those without disabilities, unless such differences can be justified.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through MAS' ongoing engagement, the insurance industry is conscious of its role to treat customers with disabilities fairly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Insurers have provided coverage without additional premiums or exclusions where autism is assessed not to pose health risks and other health conditions are not present.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For those who require care services in the community, we have places available in our 31 Day Activity Centres, eight Sheltered Workshops, four Drop-in Disability Centres, and home-based intervention services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For those who require residential services, we have 10 Adult Disability Homes and three Adult Disability Hostels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To improve access to justice, the Appropriate Adult Scheme provides trained volunteers to facilitate communication and provide emotional support during interviews between investigation officers and persons with autism, intellectual disability and/or mental health conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have rolled out measures that support PwDs seeking employment, and employers who hire PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The EEC will provide such employers with a wage offset of up to 20% of the employee's monthly income.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Additional wage offsets of up to 10% for six months will apply for long-term unemployed PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Open Door Programme or ODP, helps PwDs enter suitable jobs and integrate into the workplaces by providing support for job placement, training and cost of job redesign.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The ODP Training Grant was enhanced in July to encourage more employers to send their employees with disabilities for training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Employers can also receive funding to send co-workers of PwDs for training to build up their confidence in working with colleagues with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Job losses due to COVID-19 have impacted all Singaporeans, and we are concerned about its impact on PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are finalising plans through the National Jobs Council to further support the employability and employment of PwDs during this downturn, and we will announce more details shortly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SG Enable is growing ground-up support networks that connect care-givers to exchange best practices with one another and with professionals from SSAs and hospitals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To make it easier for PwDs and care-givers to find support and resources, SG Enable launched the Enabling Guide in 2019, a first stop portal with information on disability schemes, services and resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also plan to improve case management support for persons with moderate to severe disabilities and their families, to help them navigate the eco-system of support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Phua has also touched on a very poignant point, about the concerns families have in ensuring care for PwDs when they are no longer around.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Special Needs Trust Company or SNTC, was set up to help families with care planning and to provide affordable trust services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Much has been done to improve support for PwDs and care-givers, but definitely more can be done.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Ms Phua has noted, PwDs in the post schooling years need more learning opportunities, customised services, and supportive work environments, closer to their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will work with partners to co-create and pilot solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Ms Phua that every citizen in Singapore, regardless his/her abilities should be treated respecfully and not lose the opportunity to make choices, develop and contribute.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We aim to nurture mindsets from a young age, by improving support to children with developmental needs within preschools and promoting interaction with their peers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to involve PwDs and their families in this journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over the next two months, as part of Singapore's Emerging Stronger Conversations, we will hold more engagement sessions with PwDs and care-givers to seek views on challenges and opportunities arising from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We invite the community to co-create solutions with us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are grateful for the numerous ground-up efforts to raise awareness for inclusion of PwDs, such as the Purple Parade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are glad to see 141 employers pledging to build a more inclusive workforce in response to the President's Challenge this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will put in place support for employers to employ PwDs meaningfully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Indeed, only with the continued partnership of the people, private and public sectors, we can build a more inclusive Singapore, together.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The time allowed for the proceedings has expired.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I adjourn the House pursuant to the Standing Order.
